report.source_text: Continuous vitamin supplementation with hydroxycobalamin 1 mg/d by intramuscular route, folinic acid 10 mg/d, betaine 12 g/d and levocarnitine 3 g/d was started. In the following days, kidney function dramatically improved and hemolysis resolved (Fig. 2). Normal values of serum homocysteine and of plasma methylmalonic acid were achieved within the following month. Rituximab infusion at 375 mg/m2 was administered once a week for 4 weeks and resulted in a dramatic decrease in serum anti-factor H antibody (< 1000 UA/ml) and led to weaning from eculizumab. Six months later, the patient had no signs of hemolysis, a serum creatinine value of 75 μmol/L (eGFR 100 mL/min CKD EPI) and serum anti-factor H antibody were negative.
report.temporal_cue: following vitamin supplementation initiation and rituximab therapy

clinician.trajectory_summary: A 19-year-old woman with no prior medical history presented with weeks of asthenia and dyspnea, accompanied by hypertension (170/90 mmHg) and lower limb edema. She was admitted to the ICU with acute kidney failure and severe neurologic impairment. Initial laboratory evaluation revealed the hemolytic uremic syndrome triad: acute kidney injury (serum creatinine 246 μmol/L), microangiopathic hemolytic anemia (hemoglobin 8.9 g/dL, LDH 700 U/L, haptoglobin <0.08 g/L, schistocytes on peripheral blood smear), and thrombocytopenia (platelets 151 G/L), with significant proteinuria (7.6 g/g creatinine) and hematuria (348×10³/mL). Biochemical investigation showed markedly elevated homocysteine (285 μmol/L, normal 3.2-10.7) with normal vitamin B12 and folate levels. Genetic testing identified biallelic pathogenic variants in the MMACHC gene (c.556G>A [p.Arg189His] and c.271dupA [p.Arg91Lysfs*4]), confirming cblC deficiency. Complement pathway investigation revealed normal complement levels (CH50 109%, C3 697 mg/L, C4 153 mg/L, Factor H 106%, Factor I 95%) with no mutations in C3, MCP, factors B, H, and I genes, but anti-factor H antibody testing was markedly positive (7450 UA/mL, normal <100), confirming anti-factor H antibody-associated HUS. Treatment with hydroxycobalamin (1 mg/d intramuscularly), folinic acid (10 mg/d), betaine (12 g/d), and levocarnitine (3 g/d) was initiated, resulting in dramatic improvement in kidney function and resolution of hemolysis within days, with normalization of homocysteine and methylmalonic acid within one month. Rituximab (375 mg/m² weekly for 4 weeks) was administered, resulting in dramatic decrease in anti-factor H antibodies (<1000 UA/mL) and enabling weaning from eculizumab. At six-month follow-up, the patient had no signs of hemolysis, serum creatinine normalized to 75 μmol/L (eGFR 100 mL/min CKD-EPI), and anti-factor H antibodies became negative.
